summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to Rs 3,335.2 crore and adjusted EBITDA rose 34% to Rs 232.2 crore, but ISCS margin fell to 8.1%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 28.7% YoY and 10% QoQ, with both ISCS and GFS posting double-digit growth. Adjusted EBITDA margin was about 7%, up 30 bps YoY. ISCS margin slipped to 8.1% from 9.3% in Q4 on onboarding costs for new contracts and no Q4-style price corrections, while GFS margin rose to 4.1%. New business wins of Rs 543 crore were an all-time quarterly high and the pipeline reached over Rs 7,500 crore.

segments.name: ISCS (Integrated Supply Chain Solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 2,417 crore (+21.9% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA Rs 196.3 crore at 8.1% margin, down from 9.3% in Q4 FY26 due to implementation costs on new contracts. Management targets a return to above 9% in Q2.

segments.name: GFS (Global Forwarding Solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 918 crore (+50.6% YoY), driven by ocean freight volumes in India and higher freight rates. Adjusted EBITDA Rs 38 crore at 4.1% margin, versus 2.1% a year ago; management said it wants at least 5% over time.

guidance_outlook: Aspiration of mid-teen percentage revenue growth for FY27; management expects profit to grow faster than revenue.
Target of about 4% PBT margin; management called FY27 an aspiration and said FY28 will definitely reach 4%.
ISCS EBITDA margin expected to return to about 9% in Q2 FY27 and reach 9.5% to 10% by Q4 FY27.
GFS EBITDA margin expected at 4.5% to 5%, with management wanting at least 5%.
Early-teens EBITDA margin target referenced by an analyst; management said first 45 days of Q2 are on similar lines to Q1.
ALA JV expected to contribute revenue in H2 FY27, targeting about Rs 2,000 crore in year 5 of operations; H2 expected to be stronger than H1.
capex_capacity: Warehousing footprint about 25 million sq ft per analyst; utilisation around 85%, with room to improve through racking and automation investment.
Warehouses are largely project-driven and backed by customer contracts; depreciation on right-of-use assets rose to Rs 114 crore from Rs 93 crore YoY due to additional space for new wins.
Acquired Swamy & Sons 3PL; its results were included for 40 days of Q1 and integration is on track.
Joint venture with ALA Group for defence and aerospace: warehouse finalised, staff being trained in Italy, and warehouse certification pending before business can start in India.
Oracle ERP implemented for the India ISCS business.
demand_pricing: New business wins of Rs 543 crore in Q1 (Rs 524 crore in Q4); about two-thirds from existing customers and one-third from new logos.
Order pipeline above Rs 7,500 crore, up from Rs 6,100 crore; management expects 20-25% conversion over 12-18 months, in line with track record.
Fuel and freight cost increases are passed through to customers under contracts with some time lag; container and air cost increases also passed on.
Management expects ISCS steady-state EBITDA margin of about 8.5-9% on new contracts.
India geography revenue grew 44% YoY on record new business wins and freight volumes.
Management sees recession and geopolitical disruption as the main risk, but said it has not yet seen this playing out in customer volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ISCS EBITDA margin decline despite revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited transition and implementation costs on new contracts onboarded in Q4 and Q1, plus the absence of the Q4 customer price corrections. Management called it a one-time effect and expects margins to recover.

qa_highlights.question: How long do new ISCS contracts take to reach stable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1 to 2 quarters, depending on the contract: about 2 quarters for implant and sub-assembly work and about 1 quarter for aftermarket or finished-goods work.

qa_highlights.question: Was the GFS margin improvement due to one-offs linked to the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth came from new wins and cost optimisation through vendor consolidation, and it expects margins to stay around current levels with high double-digit growth ahead.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ALA JV revenue potential and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to about Rs 2,000 crore revenue in year 5, with first revenue in H2 FY27. It expects the JV to be margin accretive given high entry barriers and a regulated sector.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FIT 3PL merger going ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FIT 3PL will remain a separate legal entity due to GST mechanisms for certain FMCG customers. It said the entity was never part of the announced merger.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Middle East and Africa be entered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is in discussions with Middle East companies and prefers a partnership route. It said it will announce once something crystallises and is taking extra precautions due to the war.

risks_watch: ISCS margin recovery to about 9% in Q2 FY27 is the key test; management has committed to this.
Recession, geopolitical events and supply-chain disruption, with the war cited as a factor.
Container and air capacity constraints and freight rate volatility; management said costs are passed through, though with time lags.
Warehouse depreciation and lease costs rising with new space (other expenses up on short-term rentals).

key_quotes: I'm very pleased to state that both the segments delivered double -digit growth in this quarter.
You can view this as a onetime. And going forward, I don't think this will have any reflection on our future margins. It will be back to above 9%.
Whether we will reach that 4% in this year-end, I would say it's our aspiration. But FY '28 , definitely, we will be achieving our aspiration of 4%.
So, the situation, the unavailability and all of that, we see this as an opportunity also because the team works very hard with the customers to find out opportunities to meet their requirements.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, pipeline and the Q2 margin recovery, with Vikas Chadha repeatedly calling the ISCS margin dip a one-time effect. Cautious on the macro, citing recession and geopolitical risk, and evasive on the FY27 4% PBT target, which he called an aspiration.
